utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still under oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Okay. Who is on the cross-examination? It is Mr Brackovic. You are on the cross-examination. The witness is all for you. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Good morning, your Honours. Good morning, Ms Calic, and good morning to everybody else present in the court room today. Ms Calic, the last question I asked of you on Friday was whether in the months of April and May in 1992 there were armed conflicts between the TO and the HVO, on the one side, and the JNA and the Serb forces in the area of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apparently there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before these conflicts the JNA mobilised Serb volunteers and distributed arms, has it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It has.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, the Konjic municipality was part of the second military district, was it not, before the outbreak of these conflicts that I just asked you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second military district comprised a large area, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The JNA armed and organised the volunteer units in the territory of the second military district, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The size of these volunteer units was 69,198 men, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These units were organised into battalions and detachments and companies, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but there were also big differences from areas to areas, so ... but they were organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a military sense organised. The JNA distributed 51,900 pieces of weapons, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the SDS distributed 17,298 pieces of weapons, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not sure about that, but it may well be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I found this in your report. That is in one of the enclosures, document number 54, which you attached. I have not seen it before. On the basis of this information which you provided, which you confirmed and which we had an opportunity to see in the attachment, the JNA participated in the distribution of the arms with 75 per cent and the SDS with the remaining 25 per cent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is a significant armed force, is it not, Ms Calic, 69,198 men with these amount of weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct, but I should also add that also the other sides were arming their people, and you can see this from the very same report as well as from other reports, and the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia was very concerned about that fact, and also the international community, which then reacted imposing an arms embargo on the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You will agree that the JNA and the TO were the only organised armed forces in the territory of the former Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were also numerous paramilitary forces, and they were also organised to a certain extent. We should also bear this in mind. Like the Green Berets, for instance. I included a report coming from the United Nations commissions of experts. So these paramilitary forces were also organised to a certain extent. That is what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. These Green Berets. They were outside the TO and JNA with the constitution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What was the basis of their recruitment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were volunteers apparently, volunteers, and then under the law they should unify with the other forces, but in the first months they did not, but they continued to act independently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Another question I wanted to ask: when did the JNA start disarming the TO and arming the local Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It apparently started in the second half of 1991, so in the Autumn of 1991, when the war in Croatia was already on-going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is before Bosnia-Herzegovina declared itself an independent state. That is the 14th October?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, apparently, yes, but I would like to stress again also the other parties were arming their respective communities even at this time. I got also reports on this fact. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): My next question is: these volunteer units, which numbered 69,198 men, were paramilitary formations, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You speak of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the TO depot in Konjic there was 5,980 pieces of weapons belonging to the TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There are reports, yes, but maybe there were also more, you know. It's very difficult to assess how many weapons were really around. I have to rely on the reports I got, but maybe these figures are not entirely correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The former JNA was an armed force of all ethnic groups living in the former Yugoslavia; is that correct? It was composed of the members of all national groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This army only armed the Serbian people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thereby this army took an active role in the creating of the smaller rump Yugoslavia and in creating Serb-dominated Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They would argue differently, of course. They would argue that they helped the Serbs to defend themselves. Of course, this led then to the creation of a Serb para-state and to some kind of unification of different Serb-settled areas, but the JNA, I have seen no documents saying that we are creating Greater Serbia, not one single document, even not the Kideric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has it not started, these pleadings, with Garasanin and his work Nacertanije?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think so, because this was written in 1834, and they are 150 years in between. So many things changed meanwhile. Bosnia did not exist as a state. At that time it was part of the Ottoman Empire. Later on it was part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. So maybe we should not over-stress the fact that there might be a certain continuity of ideas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the Memorandum of the Serbian Academy of Science this theory was advocated, was it not, as well as in the public appearances of Voslof's "Cecel" the idea of Greater Serbia was propounded, which would extend to the west of the country up to Virovica-Karlovac-Karlobac line, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, this Memorandum of the Serb Academy of Sciences, which was written in 1986 and then published in 1987, this document has been written by a Serb intellectual, and they were complaining about alleged Serb discrimination, discrimination of Serbs, but they did not say explicitly: "Let's conquer Bosnia or Slovenia or Croatia." It was an expression of national feeling of Serb nationalists, but it was not a master-plan of creating Greater Serbia. Also you mentioned then other persons, nationalists, and I think there were many different options how this Greater Serbia could look like. It was not just one option. There were very different ideas and opinions about that. So I think we should be careful, and as for this Memorandum of the Serbian Academy of Science, it was a kind of expression of what national-oriented intellectuals were thinking at that time in the second half of the 1980s, but it was not a kind of master-plan of JNA attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, because of this idea of creation of Greater Serbia, the war in Croatia started in 1991, and a lot of fighting took place on the line which I just mentioned, did it not? Those are the facts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, there are different views on that, and I am not here to take sides or to say this is why the war broke out. I just say there were different views. You claim that the main reason for the war, the main cause, was for the greater Serb plan. The Serbs, on the other hand, would argue: "No, we just wanted to stay within Yugoslavia." So I do not want to say whether one side is correct or wrong. I would just like to explain to this court there were just different views. We should also accept this, different views.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I agree with you that there were different views. The Serbs have one version of events and the others have another one, but I am speaking about the truth. I am speaking about the facts and the facts were that there was fighting in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was fighting in 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The JNA organised volunteer units in the Konjic municipality, did it not, Ms Calic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, did you state that the Konjic municipality was located on the only railroad line and the road leading from Sarajevo to Ploci and then to Central Bosnia as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe it was a matter for translation. It was, of course, not the same road or line which led to Central Bosnia but there was a road leading to Central Bosnia from this main road, Sarajevo coast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I said from the Ploci port towards Sarajevo. That is the only main highway, which is M17; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is only one railroad line that is going from the Ploci port through Mostar, Konjic, Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In other words, we can say that these two communication lines are sort of the spine as far as the communication lines are concerned within Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Also we could say that the Konjic municipality is situated in a strategic position linking Sarajevo to Herzegovina and Central Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was, therefore, of strategic significance, as you put it in your report, and it was of significance to all the warring parties; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Konjic was an important military centre in the former Yugoslavia too; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the military industry located there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It had the plant Igman, which was one of the largest ammunition manufacturing plants in Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This plant had surface of some 20,000 square metres, and it was built underground; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Konjic municipality there are other military facilities of significance; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance the Celebici barracks, which had a large depot and facilities for large fuel storage; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then there is the Ljuta barracks, which also had underground facilities of 6,000 square metre area; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was storing the TO weaponry; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there was the barracks in Borci, which is also in the Konjic municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, you pointed an interesting thing and that is that the settlements that were predominantly Serb, like Bradina, Brdjani, Donje Selo, Celebici and Bjelovcina, that these villages were situated along this road M17, which is linking Sarajevo and Konjic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Brdani is situated, as can be seen in the map, along the railroad linking Sarajevo and Konjic; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about the JNA arming the Serbian population as well as did the SDS, that they formed volunteer units, you must have thought of these villages: Bradina, Brdjani, Donje Selo, Celebici and Bjelovcina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really. He was thinking of the Serb population as a whole because people were afraid in this municipality and other parts of Bosnia. So they distributed -- these weapons were distributed also in other areas, not only in the strategically interesting ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we can agree with the view that these arms were distributed to the Serbian population which lived in Bradina, Brdjani, Donje Selo, Celebici and Bijelovcina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were probably also weapons distributed in these areas to these villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When a moment ago we confirmed that the Serbian population was organised in military terms in platoons and detachments and companies, this also is relating to the villages that I have just mentioned; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, do you know that the JNA some time in May 1992 had an air raid on the Konjic area and four aeroplanes and helicopters of the JNA were shot down at that time? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May 1992, around May, maybe early May 1992, there was an air raid on the municipality and the city of Konjic on the part of the JNA air force, and on that occasion four aeroplanes and one helicopter of the JNA were shot down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to object to this question. It has been in detail discussed under the cross-examination done by Ms Residovic, all these attacks, and the witness has in detail stated exactly what she knew or what she could know about these attacks and stated she was not a military expert, not a "historian" for the recent happenings like these attacks. So we cannot have it, I think, your Honour, that these questions are asked once more of another defence attorney. I cannot help pointing out that for the last 20 minutes Ms Calic has said barely nothing but "correct". We are going through exactly what she has already stated. I think this repetitious way of cross-examining is not the way it should be done. Thank you, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. Mr Brackovic, can you carry on? MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I asked you whether you were aware of the fact not as a witness of the fact, as a factual witness, but as a scientist, as a historian, that in 1992 in May there were air strikes in the town and municipality of Konjic carried out by the JNA, and that on that occasion four aeroplanes and one helicopter of the JNA were shot down; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I read in some of the witness statements about air attacks and I read also that these air attacks were meant as a reaction to attacks on JNA facilities. So I am not a fact witness. I cannot say whether or not it was a reaction or whether or not it was aggression or whatever. I read in the witness statements that there were such air attacks or air raids.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was in the interest of the JNA to preserve the military industry in the municipality of Konjic, to keep all the TO armaments stored in the Ljuta barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were apparently trying, and I tried to explain this also last week, they were apparently trying to transfer these weapons to other areas, but they were not successful in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they had an interest in those weapons when you said they were trying to transfer them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think all sides involved in a war have an interest in controlling weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we can all agree that the JNA had a strategic interest in this area; is that correct, Ms Calic, to keep intact the military industry, to keep the weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The report which you quoted so many times in relation with the distribution of weapons to Serbs indicates on the contrary that they were trying to leave this area, and that they were trying to take all the weapons with them, and they simply did not manage to pull out, because they felt surrounded by Muslim and Croat forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It means that they did not leave in a disinterested manner without attempting to save the military facilities and the TO weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I do not know. This quoted report indicates that the JNA apparently was trying to transfer these weapons, to pull out personnel. Personnel was not very high in numbers. There were maybe 50, 60, maybe 80 JNA persons in this area. This is not a big number, and the very same report also says very clearly: "We are trying to pull out. We are trying to transfer weapons. We do not manage because there are so many Muslim and Croat armed forces around."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I am going to ask some questions with regard to the questions asked by my predecessor, where you did not supply detailed answers. You said that the ethnic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina was made on the basis of the Institute for Statistical Data?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These were not the data of the Institute for Statistics of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were the statistical data of the Bosnian statistical service in Sarajevo, the 1991 population census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, you stated on Friday that you wanted the report from the Institute for Statistics of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that that report was not submitted to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. I was asking for the municipal election results and these were not submitted to me. I had to provide them through other channels, through the OSC office in Sarajevo. As for the population census, I managed to find them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The map that you presented here during the examination-in-chief and the cross-examination depicting the ethnic structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is the map that I hold now in my hands; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This map does not correspond to the data existing in the Institute for Statistics of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ms Calic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It cannot be, because the municipalitites were so mixed, the villages were so mixed, if I had to indicate each and every single nation and nationality in each and every single village, we would not understand this map any more. I was trying to explain that this is just a way to reduce a very complex ethnic situation in an understandable way. I would have nothing against if you could present a better map, ethnic map. It might be helpful if you could, and I think we could easily agree on having another map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The colours indicated here on this map refer to areas where one ethnic group was in the majority, where its percentage was above 50; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It also refers to relative majority, not only to more than 50 per cent majorities; relative majorities, which might then be 40 per cent in some instances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this was not made according to the formula that this depicts the absolute majority; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Bijeljina municipality Ms Calic do you know the percentage of Serbs in the overall population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have to check this on the -- in the statistical data.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were not in the absolute majority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serbs? I just pointed out on this map you can also find relative majorities. I have to check the exact numbers. There were 109 municipalitites. I do not know them all by heart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Your Honour, on Friday I tried to show to the witness a document but since it was not in a language which is one of the working languages of the Tribunal, I had it translated on Friday. I checked this morning with the Registry, with Mr Beresford, and I was told that the document has not been translated yet. After I get this document and after your perusal of this document, I would like to ask some questions in the cross-examination of this witness, but now before that I have another set of questions, which would then conclude my cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, for your information, I can tell you that we have a translation into English of this document, which the defence lawyer has not so far got a translation of. This has been done in our investigation and there it is, this document. So if you want to have it, so I can support you with it. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I would be grateful. Do you have the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Exactly. Show it to ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: You got it also?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I got it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Do not forget to exhibit it after your cross-examination is over because you are going to question her. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): No, I will not forget. Thank you for reminding me, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: This is the English translation of the document you showed to the witness, is it? MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Yes. I believe that the witness has it in front of her now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Do you want to use it now? MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I would like to use it now. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can do so. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Decision number 28/92 of 22nd March 1992. It is the Decision of the Konjic Municipality Serbian Assembly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the decision on the proclamation of parts of the territory being exclusively Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a declaration in Serbian territories where the Serb population represents more than 51 per cent of the population and other areas where Serbs are a minority population, less than 50 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a Decision that was passed pursuant to the Decision on the verification of the proclaimed Serbian autonomous provinces in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Article 1, paragraph 3; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is not indicated in this document. The document refers to the constitution of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They also refer to the willingness of the Serbian population in the Konjic municipality that they expressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Decision is not in contravention with the Decision on the verification of the proclamation of the Serbian autonomous provinces in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You say it is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not legally contradictory to that Decision. I am not now referring the constitution -- whether this Decision is constitutional or not, but this Decision that you have in front of you is not in contradiction with the Decision on the verification of the proclaimed Serbian autonomous regions in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that so? Let me remind you that paragraph 3 states that parts of other municipalitites in this region may also be a part of the Serbian autonomous region in Bosnia; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you put it that way, yes, but it is difficult to argue in legal terms, because all these Decisions have been declared unconstitutional and unlegal, so it's a bit difficult, but it is perfectly in line with what the Serbs were doing in other areas before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would now like to go back to this map that I hold in my hands. Is this the map that you presented before this Trial Chamber as attachment number 41?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indicated in red on this map are places in which Serbs are in the majority; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we can see here, the number of those places, of those villages is ten on this map; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the Decision on Serbian territories based on the ethnic and geographical principle, where Serbs are in the majority over 51 per cent, 16 settlements were proclaimed as such; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So 6 settlements that were proclaimed as exclusively Serbian in this decision are not locations in which Serbs are in the majority in the population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you name one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One name -- well, if you have 10 here and 16 there, there is a discrepancy, 6 settlements, and these 6 settlements are the places in which Serbs were not in the majority. I will now give you a few names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am just not sure whether the map is entirely complete and whether all the very small villages are as indicated just for reasons to make -- for practical reasons. So if you could name one which is a concrete, then it would be easier for me to follow your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will give you a name. The village of Bijela. Please have a look at the map. It is indicated on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is indicated as a place where there is no ethnic majority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A Decision on Serbian territories, the village of Bijela was proclaimed as a location in which Serbs are in the majority; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would further like to ask in paragraph 2 of the decision on Serbian territories, using the principle of property in which Serbs are in the minority, in other words in locations where Serbs -- the Serbian population is less than 50 per cent, 27 villages and settlements were proclaimed as such; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But we already have a list of the areas which the Republika Srpska was claiming to be part of its territory. The constitution is before us. So I do not know really that it is necessary to go into this. We already have the detailed list. I think one of the annexures indicates the areas which the new Republic, so-called Republic, was claiming to be its own territory. I can show it to you, if you want: probably the problem occurred because in the coloured map you used the colour green a little more liberally and the colour purple less -- you use it less, which shows that all of Bosnia is a majority Muslim province. It shows that is the Serbs were really a majority, if you look at the colours of that map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are referring now to the Yugoslav map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: No, the map of Bosnia right in the beginning. I think it is annexure 3. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Ms Calic, the village of Dzepi was marked on your map as a village in which Muslims were in the absolute majority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of the Decision I quote: the Serbian people proclaimed as their territory the territory in which Serbs were in the minority; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know, because in this document they say they had attached a map with the exact borders of Serb municipalitites. So I understood that they actually claimed parts of these areas where Serbs were in a minority or where they had less than 50 per cent. Unfortunately the map, the ethnic map, is not attached to this document, and it would be much easier to argue about this or to interpret this document if we had actually this map. I believe only parts of these 27 Serb-inhabited areas were meant to be part of the Serb territory, but I am, of course, not sure, because I have not seen this map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have not seen such a map. The village of Glavaticevo was a village in which Muslims were in the absolute majority; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Glavaticevo is listed under 24 and it was proclaimed as an exclusively Serbian territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think this is not correct, because we have not seen the map. It can also be that only parts of this Glavaticevo were meant to become parts of the Serb territory. We simply do not know, because in the last paragraph of this document they say that there would be an ethnic map in which the delineated areas based on the ownership, geographic principle are drawn into. So we haven't got this map unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Grusca is also on the map that you presented here, and it was mapped as the village in which the Muslims were in the absolute majority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Grusca is listed under 26 and proclaimed as Serbian territory according to the ownership principle, and Serbs were in the minority there. They had less than 50 per cent of the population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see, we have again the same principle -- same problem, because under (2) it is indicated that these areas are areas where the Serbs are a minority population, less than 50 per cent, and there would be a map attached showing which areas exactly from these villages and areas would be considered to be Serb. So as we haven't got this map, I really cannot say whether they were claiming the entire or only part of this village. So I am afraid ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Podorasac is also a village in which Muslims were in the absolute majority according to your map, Ms Calic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The village of Podorasac was proclaimed as Serbian territory according to the ownership principle and Serbs were in a minority there, under 50 per cent of the population, and it is listed under number 17?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But maybe it was only part. I don't know. It appears that it was only part of this, you see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the decision in paragraph 2 of the decision, it does not say anything about parts of these villages being proclaimed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it says that there would be a map attached to this document showing the exact boundaries of the Serb territories. Unfortunately this map is not attached to this document, so we don't know, and I also believe that -- well, I don't believe anything, but I would like to see the map and then I could answer these questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you did not answer my question. I said that in paragraph 2 it is not said that only parts of these villages would be proclaimed as exclusively Serbian territories; is that so? Please read the text in paragraph 2 carefully.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a hint in paragraph 3. It is in the English translation. It is the delineated areas based on the ownership geographic principle, that is the ownership principle as drawn in the map of the Konjic municipality which is enclosed with this Decision. Unfortunately this ethnic map is not enclosed with this Decision, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am just now referring to paragraph 2 of the decision. It does not say anywhere that these villages are joining the Serbian territory and being proclaimed as such only partially, and you refer to paragraph 3. I am not asking you anything in relation to paragraph 3. I concentrate on paragraph 2 solely?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But I have to read the whole document. I have to understand it as a whole. I cannot just pull out one paragraph and then not read the others. I read the entire document and this is what my impression is. My impression is there should be a map and the map is important to understand this decision. Without the map you cannot fully interpret this, or not maybe correctly interpret this document. Maybe you are right, but maybe you are not. I simply do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. Buturovic Polje is a village in which Croats were in the absolute majority according to your map; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Buturovic Polje was proclaimed as Serbian territory according to the ownership principle and Serbs were in a minority there, less than 51 per cent, and that is listed under number 6; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the ethnic map -- could the ethnic map be broader than this territory, just like your map number 3?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry? I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a minute ago that it would be very hard, indeed impossible, to make a precise ethnic map of Bosnia-Herzegovina due to the mixture of the populations who lived in Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this also refer to the municipality of Konjic as regards the ethnic composition that you marked here on your map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This means that it was impossible to draw up such a map in the context that you spoke of before so that only parts of the villages referred to in paragraph 2 of the Decision on the proclamation of Serbian territories would be taken into account; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I do not -- did not understand correctly your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would mean that it would be impossible to create a map as presented under (3) if this map would only include parts of villages and settlements listed under (2); correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there would be a problem anyway because, you see, you have a problem with drawing maps only if you claim that majority having an absolute or a relative majority in a certain area means also that you should exercise power without letting participate the other nations. Once you agree on the fact that power should be shared, there is no problem any more with these simplified maps. That is why I cannot agree with your question. Even if you would be able to be more precise in drawing maps, it does not mean that one single nation, one single people, should exclusively exercise power in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This decision on the proclamation of Serbian territory based on the force of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is based on the constitution of the Serb Republic. At least, this is what is written on this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The constitution which was declared invalid by the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. Absolute correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Muslim people never declared any territories as being exclusively Muslims; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard about it; you never saw such a Decision in which the Muslim population proclaimed certain parts or portions of the Konjic municipality as exclusively their own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. However, I saw reports and I saw documents in which Serbs and also Croats were complaining that they were not allowed to participate in an appropriate way in the decision-making bodies. I also saw these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw documents in which the Croatian people proclaimed certain parts of the territory as exclusively Croatian; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exclusively. They even conceded that other nations should participate. I am not sure if this was an honest offer, but I saw these documents. I showed them, I think. I showed them and I have included them in this folder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, you said that in the beginning the war, the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was on the one side between the armed forces of the territorial defence and the HVO, and on the other side the units of the Bosnian Serbs and the JNA; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992 and even now the Serbian population which used to live and which continues to live in Bosnia-Herzegovina are all the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct? They have the status of the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina and they were stressing the fact that they were also citizens of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that they were citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Does that not mean that they do continue to be the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this is a very difficult legal question, and the international experts spent quite a lot of time in finding a solution for this, because before Yugoslavia broke apart people had two citizenships, republican, Bosnian, and then all-Yugoslav citizenship. So you reach a point where Yugoslavia falls apart and one side says: "You keep only your Bosnian citizenship"; and the other part claims: "No, we also want to keep our Yugoslav citizenship." This was a matter of debate. I am not able to say whether one or other solution was correct. It was a matter of debate and a matter of concern for the international observers. If you look now how it is regulated today under the Dayton Agreement, people are allowed to have dual citizenship. So I simply do not know whether or not in 1992 the Serbs of Bosnia were correctly considered to be only citizens of Bosnia, or whether or not they were correctly considered to be also citizens of Yugoslavia. I simply do not know. This is a question for a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you quoted the Dayton Agreement, the Bosnian Serbs cannot travel abroad on the Serb Republic passort; they can travel on the Bosnia-Herzegovina passport; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The beginning of the war in 1992 the citizenship of Bosnian Serbs as Bosnians was not controversial, and the citizenship of Yugoslavia was not negated; correct? At that time Bosnia was an internationally-recognised state as of 6th April 1992 by the European Community, on 7th April by the US and Croatia and shortly thereafter by a large number of states; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is correct that the country was recognised in April 1992, but it is also true that on the contrary the question of citizenship was a matter of debate and it was contested, and the Serbs continued to claim that they wanted to continue to be citizens of Yugoslavia. So it was a matter of debate at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The referendum that the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina organised was based on the recommendations of the international community; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The number of votes which made up the absolute majority, which was the basis for the proclamation of independence, was an expression of the will of the majority of the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This gives me the opportunity to show you the exact figures of the referendum. There was a question last week. I got the exact figures, and if you allow me, I just want to show them. Can I have the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: It is not one of the documents included in this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I found it over the weekend, just, because there was this question about the exact figures, and we can see that from 64 per cent of valid voting papers there were 99.44 per cent of voters in favour of independence while only 0.29 per cent voted against. Then there were a minor number of spoiled voting papers. The reason why I said we can assume that one-third of the population was, in fact, against independence is that there was a call for a boycott by the SDS, and there was also a so-called plebiscite by the Serbs a few months ago in which, on the other hand, the majority of Serbs expressed the will to remain in Yugoslavia. Of course this plebiscite has never been recognised by the international community, and we do not know the exact terms on which it was held. What we know is that the Serbs then afterwards proclaimed that -- declared that more than 1 million Serbs had voted during this plebiscite in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia. So this I cannot confirm. I cannot confirm whether or not this referendum by the Serbs was correctly organised. This is just an indication to show to us that probably many Serbs were against independence. They held their own plebiscite, and they did not want to participate in this one, because at this time they contested already the legitimacy of Muslims and Croats deciding over the future of their country. The SDS simply said: "We do not agree on everything you decide on the republican level, so we just boycott", and there was a corporate boycott. So if you ask me if there was a majority vote in terms of numbers, yes. In terms of having -- in terms of how many were against, we can assume maybe one third was against. Maybe less but let us assume one third. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): The international community recognised the results of the referendum in which the majority of the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina voted for a sovereign and independent Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, in a number of UN resolutions the participation of the JNA has been characterised -- the JNA as well as the FRY -- has been characterised as foreign powers, and sanctions were imposed on this country which lasted for three or four years; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, based on the international law in this situation when we have the Bosnian Serbs and the JNA on the one side, as well as the state of Yugoslavia, the participation of the Bosnian Serbs in such war and aggression can be perceived as an armed rebellion; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let's say this is at least a matter of debate, and I think it is also a question for a lawyer, because, as I was pointing out many times, the Serbs believed that they were part of Yugoslavia, and they created the parallel institutions. They created their army on the territory of Bosnia. They created their state institutions. So this is a very difficult question to be put to a lawyer -- yes, to a lawyer, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to introduce the document that Ms Calic just presented and which she said that she had not used previously, and I would like it marked as evidence. This is the number of people who had taken part in the referendum, and I would like to offer it in evidence. I would also like to ask a question relating to this document. Has this document been submitted to the prosecution before? It has, has it not, Ms Calic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The document on the referendum, you mean? Which document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you showed earlier. You said that you found this subsequently, that you had not included it before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The referendum one?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. In other words, if I understood you correctly, you had shown it before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Earlier you said that it would be a complex legal issue. My question to you is: should Lugican Serbs in Germany ask for an exclusive Serbian territory and rule and would want to accede to other Serbs in Yugoslavia, the German authorities would treat it as an armed rebellion, would they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But the Serbs in Germany do not have German citizenship. We cannot compare. Sorry. The migrants, the Serb migrants in Germany, they continue to have their respective Yugoslav or Croat or whatever citizenship. Most of them are not German citizens.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may not have understood me, Ms Calic. My question was the Lugican Serbs, which is a national minority living in Germany, they have been living there for tens and hundreds of years there. I was referring to them. They have German citizenship, but ethnically they are of Serbian origin. So if these Serbs wanted to proclaim certain territories where they live as Serbian and secede from Germany and accede to Yugoslavia, German State or authorities would consider that an armed rebellion; Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Look, the German constitution is very much different from the Bosnian and from the former Yugoslavian one, because Germany consists of one state nation, which are the Germans. Then there are a number of minorities, which have certain minority rights, but these persons are not supposed to be constituent nations of Germany, whereas in Bosnia there were three constituent nations and in the constitution as well as many laws there was a principle implemented. This principle said: "Important decisions should be made with the consent of the three constituent nations." So at least if one withdraws, if one is not consulted any more, if one decides not to participate any more, you have a problem as for the implementation of the constitution, as for the implementation of many laws. In Germany the situation is, of course, different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me give you have another example. If the Celts in Germany wanted to secede from Germany, people of Celtic origin, the German state would consider this as an armed rebellion; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. We never got this problem, so ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that you had no such problems, but if you did have them, they would be treated as rebels; correct. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If, for instance, Bavaria, which is one of the republics of Germany, would decide to leave the country, then we might get a similar problem to the Yugoslav problem. If we had one minority just trying to secede I don't know, because we never got this problem, and I think we will never get this problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a historian. If the Friesian people in the Netherlands wanted to secede and form their own state, would that not constitute an armed rebellion?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am sorry. I cannot keep silent any longer. These hypothetical questions are not to be asked to an expert on the former dissolution of Yugoslavia. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I will not ask further questions along these lines, but I left this for the end. Your last name, "Calic", is a bit unusual for a German citizen; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know, because there are so many names. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much, Mr Brackovic. I think we’ve got carried on in this way for quite a long time . We will break now and reassemble at a quarter to 12. (11.25 am) (Short break) (12.45 pm) JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Mr Brackovic, frankly I have not been able to estimate the extent of your cross-examination because I do not even though where you are going. You know where you are going. Will you be able to try to get it over within the longest or shortest possible time, please. We have had the same thing over and over for so long. So let us get to the end of it. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I think I will come to the close very soon, your Honours. Before I continue with the cross-examination, the defence would like to offer to the Trial Chamber in evidence the document that Ms Calic showed and explain the situation on the referendum, and the defence would like to use it as evidence, and is offering it to the Trial Chamber in evidence, and also the defence offered the document that has been translated into English as evidence as well, and so I would like to -- I would like the Trial Chamber to rule on this exhibit. I would also like to mention that on Friday the document that was offered was marked as D-3/4. So if you would please rule on this. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Very well. Thank you. I think you have distributed the document? Have you distributed it already, because I have not seen any of them? MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): Does the Trial Chamber accept this exhibit, the document of Ms Calic and the document that the defence would like to offer in evidence? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Well, I might have misunderstood you. I thought you said you had already produced the documents. The document which you translated was your own document, not that of Dr Calic. So it could not have been your own. Although you can tender it through her, it is not a defence document. If you have any other document which you think is relevant, you pass it on. The prosecution will look at it. They have no objections. You can still take her through it. If you follow that pattern in the documents in the proceedings having to be also marked as an exhibit. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I would like to request if -- with your permission I would like my colleague, Ms McMurrey, to explain this, because she is coming from a Common Law legal system, and she would be able to better explain how we are trying to tender this. So would you allow Ms McMurrey to present this and say a few words? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Of course she can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. We would like to offer two documents from Mr Brackovic's cross-examination into evidence. They are both documents that came -- one came from the prosecutor himself. It was the English translation of the document that Mr Brackovic had tried to introduce on Thursday. So the prosecution is well aware of it. They have had time to examine it, and we would like to have that document marked as defence exhibit and offer that into evidence. Ms Calic was cross-examined from that document. The second document, of course, is the document that Ms Calic did not introduce into evidence as part of her package, which is the document that shows the figures and the breakdown on the vote in the referendum on March 1st. We would also like to have that marked as defence exhibit. She was cross-examined from it. The prosecutor was well aware of it. He has seen the document before today. We would like to tender that to the court for evidence also. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Now let us be clear about this: was the document part of the whole package?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I mean, the document which you say is the second document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: It is not one of the documents in this package?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: No,, your Honour, it is not. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: How did it become her own document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: She brought it after perusing through her documents at the weekend to clarify some things. We think it is important evidence for the court to review later. We would like to offer it into evidence as a defence exhibit. So we are offering two documents from this cross-examination. We would like to have both admitted into evidence. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: That is perfectly proper. You can tender them.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: We have no objection to it, your Honours. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Where are the documents themselves? I have seen only one. The interpretation, I have seen that. I have not seen the second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was the one that was on the ELMO earlier. It is the document showing the breakdown of the vote during the referendum on March 1st. I think Ms Calic probably has it in her possession. We need the usher to take it from Ms Calic and have it marked by Mr Roeland, please. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please, let us get it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: These documents will be document D-3/4 for the Declaration and D4/4 for the document on the referendum. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You can carry on. MR BRACKOVIC (in interpretation): I would only like to pose several questions which I would like to sum up. There are only three or four of them, and that would complete my cross-examination. Ms Calic, the Konjic municipality is part of Bosnia-Herzegovina which has been proclaimed an independent and sovereign state; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The state of Bosnia-Herzegovina is a common state of all constituent people living in it; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is composed of two parts. One is the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the other is Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Konjic municipality is a multi-ethnic community; correct? It consists of members of all three nationalities, with a majority Muslim population; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you speaking of today?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am talking about the situation of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pursuant to the Decision on the Serb territories, 28/92 of 22nd March 1992, representatives of the Serbian population wanted in an illegal way to separate out a part of the territory of the sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina as their own territory, and they wanted at that time to accede to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at that point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They set up their parallel state structures and they apparently wanted to be part of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They wanted to make it part of Yugoslavia; in other words, they wanted it to be part of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In their words they wanted to remain in Yugoslavia. This is how they would put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms Calic. I would also like to thank the Trial Chamber. My cross-examination is complete with respect to Ms Calic. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you very much. Cross-examination by MR GREAVES

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: May it please your Honour, on behalf of Mr Mucic I would like to ask just a few questions of Dr Calic, if I may, please. Dr Calic, I would like you to focus, please, for a moment on the period between spring of 1992 and winter of 1992 in the Konjic area. The war began in the spring effectively?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The consequences for the administration of the Konjic area was, as I understand what you have told us, the disintegration of the conventional peacetime civil lines of authority and military chains of command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is replaced by what is described as the War Presidency, which is an organisation brought together at very short notice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be right to describe the period we are talking about as one which was to a large degree rather chaotic in terms of administration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Chaotic -- I do not know whether it was chaotic in this sense. I would describe -- maybe let us put it like this: this was a certain power vacuum. There were laws, there were regulations, but there was some uncertainties and some doubts as to whether and as to which extent these laws and regulations were implemented on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed who, in fact, is exercising real power?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By that it may well be that those who are named as members of the War Presidency did not, in fact, wield de facto power?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe. I do not know. This is up to the witnesses to explain to the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absolutely. I will come back to that aspect in a moment, if I may. The situation you described to us is one which essentially exists on paper, and that is how you have been able to reach your conclusions, by examining, as it were, the records?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the reality on the ground, and I think you have effectively conceded this, may well be very different from that which is portrayed by the paperwork?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from those organisations which are recorded as existing on paper, there may well be other, for example, ad hoc groups that come together for very short periods, which exercise influence and authority?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which are not documented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed any decision which on the face of it, on the face of the paperwork, is promulgated by the War Presidency may well have been promoted by some other group of influence within the Konjic area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you help me about this: the paperwork from the Konjic municipality for that period that you have examined, would you describe it as extensive, in other words, a lot of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was some of it. I was unfortunately not able to get hold of all these documents. I was trying since December last year. Unfortunately none of these documents have been submitted to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but those documents that you have been able to examine, would it be right to, as it were, categorise them as paperwork which records decisions of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were also decisions by the municipality. There were also other documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I was going give you some examples. Documents recording the appointments of people to particular jobs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some correspondence between the municipality and other parts of the country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And internal correspondence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Among others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And documents setting out policy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the reality: that you could assess from looking at those documents, that, in fact, the bureaucracies, whatever the chaotic conditions, may have been, as in so many of these sorts of situations -- the bureaucracies carried on generating the paperwork; in other words the civil service side of it carried on working, generating the paperwork, recording decisions, recording appointments and that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some decisions in line with the laws and regulations. There were others which appeared to me that they were made on an ad hoc basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It appeared also to me that there were different power centres present in this, emerging in this situation. So as for administration, I mean administration is one part of the whole set-up. It is not the entire. There are other power centres, military, maybe non-military as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, Dr Calic, but the point I was putting to you is this, that whatever and whoever was running the show, the people whose duty it is to record the decisions continued to work and record those decisions and appointments and so on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Indeed, from the documents you have examined would you agree that there has been quite a high degree of preservation of important documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I think there must have been much more documents, much more than I was able to look at, I was able to get hold of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am perfectly prepared to agree that. You obviously have not seen the lot, but from what you have seen, a reasonable degree of information has been preserved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just finally ask you this: it is really in relation to your qualifications, if I may just return to that. Could you just identify to the Tribunal the precise name of this think-tank for which you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is Stiftung Wissenschaft und Politik; Research Institute for International Affairs would be the English translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You took the next question out of my mouth, Dr Calic, and I am grateful to you for doing so. Does it come to this: your job is essentially the analysis of military defence and foreign intelligence for your masters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not really. We are independent researchers. We are allowed to choose our subjects by our own and we are choosing also our sources by ourselves. So I have, in fact, a broad variety of different sources which I use for my daily work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do various German ministries come to you and ask for your analysis of a particular situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This may happen, but it often happens that I choose by myself and I just try to identify important subjects and important developments and then make them attentive and try to draw the attention to certain developments. So it is more or less that I by myself -- it is my task myself to assess the situation and then identify important issues on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom do your reports normally go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our reports go to different addressees. Some are the ministries. It is the Chancellor's Office, but it is also Members of Parliament. It is sometimes other universities, other scholars, other institutes. It is sometimes the media. It really depends on the subject and on the character of the report. Not everything is for everybody, but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr Calic. That is all I have to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have one question before cross-examination of the defence is completed. The Prosecution just passed out, while Mr Brackovic was finishing his cross-examination, some documents. I do not know if it is their intention to use them now on re-direct examination, but if it is, I think everybody would like a opportunity to review these before we capitulate at this point. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Let us hear the prosecution. What document is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: These documents are produced to satisfy Madam Residovic for her remaining questions. She had reserved the right after the review of the documents we have given to her, to continue her cross-examination. So that is what we have produced these documents for, but at the end of it, we are going to tender them as evidence, together with the bundle we have before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: That makes it clear for me. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: It is Mrs Residovic's intent to follow up the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: Yes. If she does not use all of them, I will have them put to Dr Calic. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Then, Ms Residovic, it is up to you. Cross-examination by MRS RESIDOVIC (resumed) MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honour. I will now use my right, having received the documents from the prosecution, to ask some more questions of Ms Calic. Your Honour, Mr Ostberg, the representative of the Prosecutor, distributed five documents to us. I think that these are the documents that were supposed to be the basis for the drafting of attachment 50 of the expert witness, and I would, therefore, ask you, if these documents are not in the possession of the expert witness and the Trial Chamber, that these documents be distributed to you now in the English language, which would facilitate my asking these questions. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: They have not been distributed. I do not know why they have not been.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: They will immediately be distributed, your Honour. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): The defence has made copies. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I know that the practice here is that all documents intended to be tendered are distributed prior to the date of tender. So if you had that in mind, obviously you should have distributed them as you decided to send them to Ms Residovic. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you very much. Good day, Ms Calic. I would ask you to put on the ELMO your chart of the defence of Konjic, number 50. My question -- that would make my questions easier to understand for all of us. I can see the chart on the monitor. Please allow me to remind you that on 19th March in the course of this trial, listed on pages 760 and 761 of the transcript, I asked you of the sources on which you base your knowledge of Konjic, and you replied to me that unfortunately you only had certain documents in your possession presented to you by the prosecutor, and that you missed some other documents pertaining to Konjic. Do you remember that, Ms Calic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it slightly different. I remember, and this is also what I want to repeat here, that I saw many, many, many documents, and I handed over -- I just made a choice of a few of them, which were the basis of this diagram, defence planning. I saw many, many others supporting this diagram. So this is just a few documents to show you the kind of documents I used. What I was then saying, moreover, is that unfortunately the respective authorities in Konjic and in Sarajevo were not able to provide me with some official documents from the Konjic municipality. For instance, the local gazette of the War Presidency and so on, I have requested this. I have not got them, and this is what I would have liked to see moreover, but I really think I had quite a lot of documents available to base this diagram on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since in addition to your report you submitted to us a certain number of regulations in existence before the war, as well as regulations passed during the war pertaining to the defence, as far as I can remember, on Thursday, 20th March I asked you whether these were the only documents, and the response was that you also had some other documents in mind, and now I ask you, since you see now that the prosecutor submitted five documents to us, are these the documents that you had in mind when you made this scheme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had these as well as many, many other documents in mind when I drew this diagram. This is just a selection of a few of the documents which all together confirmed this view or support this view.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, Ms Calic, despite the fact that we asked you to submit all the documents to us, the prosecutor submitted only a selection of the documents, of your documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I submitted only a selection of these documents, because they are something like maybe several hundreds, and these documents I believe will be introduced during the trial. They will be introduced by other witnesses. I just wanted to present you with a selection of documents which are representative for many other documents which I have seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms Calic, I remember very clearly what my request was. I wanted to have all your documents pertaining to the drawing-up of this chart, which would enable me to evaluate whether this chart was based on certain regulations or documents that would be relevant to the making of this chart. Are you able to provide us with all those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the documents which I selected are maybe enough to explain this diagram. If not, I can, of course, find in addition more documents supporting it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I start asking you some questions, I would like to ask you, Ms Calic, if you could just clarify to me what this chart means, the chart that forms the attachment number 50?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I will. So first I draw the War Presidency. I knew from former regulations and law that this institution existed. Then I saw a number of documents signed by representatives from the War Presidency. So I concluded there was a War Presidency in Konjic. So I assumed there is a War Presidency. Then I knew there was -- separate from this War Presidency there was a military structure. I knew this also from the official gazettes that there was at least a separate military structure existing. I saw numerous documents coming from the Konjic municipality which were signed either by the HVO, the Croat Army, or by the TO or the Bosnian Army, which represented at this time the Muslim defence forces. I knew also that there was a law and -- there was a regulation in April and then a law in May saying that all defence forces should be unified, but I knew from what was going on on the ground that this did not succeed entirely, but they remained two separate structures, a Croat and a TO. So I knew moreover that there was a general policy at this time of acting together, so the Croat and the Muslim defence forces usually acted together, but they did not act as a unified force. They acted by making decisions together. I presented some documents which show that some of the orders or some of the decisions taken were actually signed by both commanders, the commanders of the HVO and the commander of the TO. So I drew up the two different structures and I linked them, because I knew many decisions were taken jointly, and then there was also even a joint staff established. I submitted documents from which we can see that they signed a joint staff TO/HVO. Furthermore, I found a document from May, which is also included in this package, which showed me there was a coordinating instance. This was the co-ordinator here in the middle. Now, I do not know of any law or regulation defining what a co-ordinator exactly is. I assume there is no such law which would define the role of a co-ordinator, but I knew from this very interesting document of the JNA and from everything which I knew before about all people's defence that such functions existed, and please allow me to put this document again here on the ELMO. It shows us how all people's defence was perceived at this time. It speaks about shared responsibilities.
