utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The conditions were bad and the building itself was used as a fire-fighting equipment storage facility. There was a pump there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were there the second time can you describe the food and the other facilities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The other conditions were really very bad. There was some food, but at first, the first eight days, I couldn't eat at all, because I bled a lot and the doctors there, the prisoners, they were struggling to stop the haemorrhage and they finally managed to do that. So for eight days I couldn't get up myself. The others had to help me. If I lay on my back, I couldn't even get up. So that I was really in a very, very bad way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there ever a time when you were at the camp when you were in a condition such that you could eat but food was not available? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please can we break here? Perhaps you will construct your sentences a little better when we come back. We will return at 4.15. (3.50 pm) (Short break). (4.15 pm). JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Please kindly remind the witness he is still under his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: A reminder that you are still under oath, sir. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Counsel, this kind of questions, witness is here for you to guide him instead of leading him. Guide him. He will state what he is here to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I will try to guide without leading. Mr Gotovac, what, if anything, do you know concerning who was in charge of Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We heard and I saw him there, Pavo Mucic, Zdravko. Pavo is his nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you hear that he was in charge from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All the ones who knew him said that, and I knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever see Mucic when you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, especially when I was in number 22, as a patient. He walked in there. He came to number 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the infirmary did anyone ever ask how it was that you were injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they didn't, only during the visit of the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- during the visit of the International Red Cross who was it who asked you how you were injured? Persons from the camp or persons from the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Persons from the Red Cross through an interpreter, who was a short woman from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, you showed us the injury on your hand. Do you have any other visible injuries anywhere on your body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have in the abdominal area and it's protruding quite a bit, and my shoulder also is deformed pretty much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you receive the injuries that caused your abdominal and shoulder problems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From hangar number 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the beatings that you have already told us about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object. She is leading again.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I would like to say guiding.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I am objecting to the leading form of the question again, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I will rephrase the questions. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, what happened in front of hangar number 6 such that you have abdominal and shoulder injuries. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He did not say anything happened in front of number 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I am sorry, I believe he did. I just asked: where did you receive the injuries? His answer was: "From hangar number 6". JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He has already replied to the question and he says he was beaten up. Why do you want it again?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Because, your Honour, I am going to ask -- I have just obtained the defence counsel's permission, and I am going to ask -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You are wanting to tell the Trial Chamber how he got this injury.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Ask him: "How did you get your injuries?"

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: How did you get your injuries, Mr Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I was taken out I got injuries in the abdominal area from kicking and also from -- and also with the fist. He was waving it and just hitting me always in the same time. Then when he hurt me he said -- and I held on to my side and he said: "Why are you holding it?" I said: "Something snapped in there." He said: "Now I am going to operate on you."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is he, so the record is clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Esad Landzo, called Zenga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, would you consent to someone from the video photograph unit of the Tribunal taking photographs of your injuries later on this afternoon so that they can be shown to the court? The defence council has previously agreed to this being done, your Honour. Would that be all right with you, Mr Gotovac? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: He has only mentioned one injury and he has only spoken of just one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Did he have any other injuries apart from the one he has just told the Trial Chamber about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I should have pictures taken of the shoulder and the arm and the abdominal area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the hand -- the video unit has come down to say that the video showing the palm of the hand injury did not come out well because of the limitations of the video equipment. So we would be asking that pictures of all these injuries be obtained, and defence council has already agreed to this during the break. Mr Gotovac, were you ever told why you were being imprisoned in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard nothing except that it was because I was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever interrogated at all while you were at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On one occasion there was Miro Stenek. It was very little. He saw that my throat was hurting and asked just a few questions. He said: "Are you an SDS member?" I said: "No." "Do you have any arms?" I said: "No." He said: "Just go away. You're not important."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when it was that Mr Stenek interviewed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Early June 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign a statement at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I didn't have my glasses, so I never read it, so I don't know what it is about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever interviewed or interrogated at any other time while you were at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zravko Mucic came on 29th August and told me that I was not questioned, and I told him that I was questioned by Miro Stenek, but very briefly. He said: "He did not", and then he called me in and he saw what my situation was, and he said: "Number 8." I didn't know what it was. That was category 8, which means that you didn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened next after you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said: "Go lie down", and I went there and in the 30th in the evening I was called out to go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you then released on 30th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly on 30th August around 9. I had no watch but that was the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the usher's assistance, I would like to show the witness an exhibit and get it marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: What is this about?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: This is his release diagram, which has already been shown to defence counsel, and I have extra copies for the court. I would ask that the originals of the document and the translation be marked as prosecution exhibit 75 and 76. I am sorry. I have been corrected. 75 and 75A for the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The original I can understand but why are copies getting exhibited?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Well, in this particular case the only -- the copies are for your Honours' and the legal officer's convenience. In this case this is a case where we actually have the original document, although I warn the court there are going to be other cases which are different, but in this case we have the original document which is being shown to the witness and then copies are being supplied to your Honours' convenience. Can you please show him 75? Mr Gotovac, you are being shown what has been marked for identification purposes as Prosecution Exhibit 75. Can you look at that document that is next to you on the instrument, Mr Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what that is, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is the release document of 30th August 1992 from number 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But it mentions the date 19th September? Oh, that is his date of birth. I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is my date of birth.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, is this the document you received when you were released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you know, whose signature is on the document? Who signed it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I assume that it is Mucic, but I can't see it that well, because he said: "Village of Celebici?" I said: "Please, sir, I am not from Celebici. I am from Viniste, near Homolje" and then he made the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I believe he was just explaining that Mr Mucic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If he did not see it, how can he identify the signatures?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Did anyone write or sign anything on the document while you were there, Mr Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean at 22? No. The first time it was written that way. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: At the time you were released did anyone sign anything to release you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain you. I just got a release paper, no other document.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Who gave you have the release paper?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mucic, Zdravko Mucic gave it to me. His nickname is Pavo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any discussion with Mr Mucic about what should be on the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Except when he said Celebici, but I had a cousin in Celebici, so I told him I was not from Celebici. I was from Viniste. So he put in a correction. That is all he did, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, at this time I would move into evidence Prosecution Exhibit 75 and 75A, which is the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: The defence of Esad Landzo has no objections to that exhibit, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: There being no objection to the exhibits, they are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I thank the International Criminal Tribunal -- I would like to express my thankfulness for allowing me this opportunity to give my evidence here and I think that it is good that people know what I have gone through and what I have suffered, me and my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Were his sons also released along with him or did they just stay? Just off the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir. I do not know the answer to that question. Sir, when were your sons released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One stayed seven months and the other one eight after me. When I was released from Celebici to the sports hall in Konjic they were moved there and then they were released from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One second, please. No more questions, your Honour. Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: That is all you have for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The witness is now available for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, cross-examination will proceed in this way: first, counsel for Mr Mucic; second, counsel for Mr Landzo; third, counsel for Mr Delic; and fourth, counsel for Mr Delalic. Cross-examination by MR GREAVES

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: May it please your Honour. Mr Gotovac, I want to ask you, please, about the time when you were released from the camp at Celebici. That was at the end of August of 1992. Prior to that you had an interview with Mr Mucic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was one of only a few occasions when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one of the few occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is right, is it not, that you only saw him in the period shortly before your release?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, not often, but I did see him then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the only times that you saw him were in the month of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In August 1992, on 29th August 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry, Mr Gotovac. May I clarify, please, that you only saw Mr Mucic in the month of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him before, but not often. On that occasion on 29th August 1992 he was in number 22, inside the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that when you saw him in number 22, that was in the month of August of that year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 30th August 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the day before your release you were interviewed by Mr Mucic in the presence of a lady secretary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Her name was Ismeta. I don't know her last name. She was a typist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that she was a typist because she typed up what you were saying during the course of the interview; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. She used the typewriter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the length of time that your interview took was about ten minutes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, even shorter than that. It was a really very short interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a formality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How would he know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, since he did not recognise the questioning that was conducted by the man whose name is Miro Stenek, he didn't want to agree that I was questioned by him. So he just asked me a couple of questions, and he said to his typist: "8", and then the doctors asked me: "What did you get?" I said: "I don't know. He said something 8." Then they said: "Well, it's good news. You are going home", and that is what happened. I was released the next day, on the 30th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it right that at about the same time that you were interviewed someone else that you know was also being interviewed, Nedjo Kuljanin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nedjo Kuljanin was also not questioned because he was in the hospital in Jablanica, because he had been injured. He was also assigned category 8. After his turn it was my turn to go in. We were together in number 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nedjo was also released at the same time as you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on 30th August 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other detainees released on 30th August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several remained after we left in 22. There were 12 beds there. It was a small place. They were wooden beds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from you and Nedjo, were other people released at the same time as you, Mr Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Some people were released before me, Petko Mrkajic, the doctor; then Dr Grubac Petko, and then also a man by the name of Savo Djordjic. I don't recall because I didn't know all of these people. I don't know when they were released exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even though you may not be able to recall the names of those released, can you recall how many people were released at about the same time as you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That night Nedjo Kuljanin and myself and the ones that I mentioned just now, they were released before. I mean the two doctors and Savo Djordjic, he was also released before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there others whose names you did not know who were also released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because I did not know people's names and because I was very seriously ill, I was in bed all the time, and sometimes I would even pull the covers over my head. I can't recall who was released when. I remember precisely for these people but not for the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having been released, did you go back to your home village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent a night at Nedjo Kuljanin's in Donje Selo and the next day I went slowly back to my village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr Mucic come to your village at all after you had been released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not come to Vinjiste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, do you remember the first visit of the Red Cross to the camp in early August 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. We were visited on 12th August 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have a document pertaining to that. I think I handed it over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the first visit that you can recall made by the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in the 22 and number 6, when I went from the 22 to the 6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In August 1992 would you accept that the conditions of feeding and provision of medicine improved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There were some medicines, and as for the food, well, we who were sick, maybe we got some more because we were so weak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, I would like to ask you now about the time of your detention, when you were arrested and taken to the camp. When you were arrested, did those who were arresting you search you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not search me, because a neighbour of mine, Emir Alic, he told me that someone who come in the morning and the village would be searched, and he told me to go to his place so he can give me shelter. My younger son went to Dervo Bajic and Spasoje Miljevic. I was here. In the evening the police came. They wore camouflage uniforms and white belts. They arrested me and Spasoje and my younger son and they took us to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were arrested, did you have any items of value on you, such as a watch or money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, I would like you, please, to look at a short piece of video, one that we have already played to another witness, and tell me if there is anybody that you recognise on that video, please. Your Honours, it is the short piece of video that you have already seen with people on it. (Videotape played).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see Mirko Kuljanin. He is from Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anybody else that you recognise amongst those people on the film?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Please, my sight is not so good. I can see people, but because my sight is so poor, I cannot recognise people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Just a minute. When was this video obtained or prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour. I did not hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When was this video prepared?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know if this was taken in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe it is on 20th August. In fact, if you look at the monitor now, you will see the date and indeed the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: And it was taken by whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: By Mr Mucic and it was recovered from his home address in Vienna upon his arrest. Does that help your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: My pleasure. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Ms McMurrey, I think it is for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Cross-examination by MS McMURREY.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May it please the court. Good day to you, Mr Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good day to you too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Cynthia McMurrey and I am defence attorney for Esad Landzo. On 22nd February 1996 you visited and talked with the investigators from the prosecution, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 22nd? Sorry. I did not understand you. What month are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On February 22nd, 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in Temisvara.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you came to testify here in The Hague someone from the Prosecutor's Office notified you that the defence attorneys would like to visit with you too, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We spoke very briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you refused to speak to anybody from the defence side, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I was not very happy. I avoid things like that, because my hearing is poor. I did not have my hearing aid the way I have it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you refused to give us the same courtesies that you offered the prosecution; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not refuse. I don't see what it is that I refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You refused to talk to us, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not refuse. I could not hear very well, but we did talk for some time very shortly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the prosecution told you that you refused to talk to us, would they be misrepresenting the facts?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I object and -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Do you not think it is easier not to antagonise this witness. Go on with whatever questions you have.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Gosh! Your Honour, I do not know with all the questions I have that I can go through my cross-examination without antagonising. I will do my best. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Better try not to. It is safer for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will try not to. Mr Gotovac, did you refresh your memory before testifying today with any document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what documents you mean. I gave all the documents that I had in my possession.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am specifically asking: did you re-read your prior statement that you made on February 22nd 1996?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It took me a while to read it, but I did read through it, because my sight is not very good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling the court today that your hearing is not very good and your sight is not very good; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it is my age. I am 65 years old, and due to all the torture that I have been through this is not really very strange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr Gotovac, when you were preparing for your testimony today you did meet with some people from the prosecutor's office, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what meetings you are talking about. We just discussed some things here in the waiting room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you were discussing the things before you were testifying today in the waiting room, was -- let us say was Ms McHenry present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, she was, if we are now talking about the prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is Ms McHenry's position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I guess she's the judge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Did she meet with you when you were -- when you had this meeting with Ms McHenry, was your investigator there, the one you spoke to when you were in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The journalist, Branca, who spoke to me in Bosnia, she was not here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was it just you and Ms McHenry? Is that what you are telling the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the interpreter, Zivkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You testified before that -- I believe you were born in Konjic, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Bjelovcina, about 8 kms from Konjic and I lived in Konjic. I had an apartment there in Konjic. I lived there for a long time, and when I retired, I went to live in the country in the village of Vinjiste and I built a summer house there, and I lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You lived in Vinjiste or did you live in Homolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is fifteen minutes walk between the two villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which village did you have live in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very close neighbourhood, in Viniste.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. You are a Bosnian Serb national, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you never claimed to be anything other then a Bosnian Serb, have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, nobody ever forced me. I was never in a position to change anything. I always was what I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, the March 1st 1992 referendum, where the Bosnians voted for their independence, you either voted or you could have voted in that election, could you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't really remember that referendum all that well. I don't remember where I was. I didn't vote. Nobody forced me to vote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you could have voted, if you wanted to, could you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could have, but nobody really told me about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, are you a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I always stated that I was not and nobody forced me to be a member because of my age. Because of my age I was not involved in anything, and, in fact, I never in my entire life was involved in anything. I was not a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying you were not politically active whatsoever in 1992; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that no, you were never active politically in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was not active.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, you were convicted of an offence before in Bosnia, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not even 40 years ago?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must object.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: A conviction 40 years ago can have no possible relevance to this case and I believe for protection of the witnesses, both under rule 75 and I believe 95, to bring up issues such as convictions that occurred 40 years ago would be improper in most national systems that I am familiar with, and I certainly think it should be not permitted before this Tribunal. There is a limit, I believe, to what the witness can fairly be cross-examined about, about what is relevant to their credibility for witnesses, and I object.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will withdraw the question. Unless he stated he was convicted of perjury, you are absolutely right. It would be irrelevant. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Tell me: what is the business of the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Because I was informed he did have a prior conviction. None of us -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: In respect of what?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I did not know what it was. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You should not have offered it, unless you knew what the conviction was about. You see, this is what counsel should learn to accept. You can go to justify what you are saying after that. You should never have said it. You cannot now go further to justify the type of conviction. He has said no, he has no convictions.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I accept his answer, but because we were not allowed investigation of the witnesses ahead of time I have no way to go back and pull up any records from that area. What this is is investigation by trial because we had no way to find out the background of these witnesses. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I tell you we are now dealing with the objections to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: And I accept the objection. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I withdraw the question. As I said, it is not relevant unless it was a perjury conviction and I had no idea. So thank you. Mr Gotovac, you are a neighbour of Mirko Babic, are you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We were born in Bjelovcina together and I left 25 years ago. So we did not meet much. We did not work together. He was a forester. So since we did not meet we did not have an opportunity to find out much about one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you have remained friends over the years, have you not? I am sorry. I have did not hear the interpretation? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Actually, what was the answer? I did not hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I did not either. I am not getting anything on interpretation. We have lost it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear me now? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you have the witness repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I think the question was: you and Mirko Babic have remained friends, though, have you not? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. That was the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We never quarrelled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is a negative answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gotovac, you have seen Mirko Babic and you have visited with him since you left Bjelovcina 25 years ago, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him seldom, because we were on very -- we had different kinds of jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mirko Babic since you have been in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were visiting with Mirko Babic here in The Hague, you discussed your testimony with him, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not talk to him, but I saw him when he was going back to the airport to get on the plane to go home. I did not have an opportunity to talk to him, because we each had our own rooms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that since August of 1992 you have never talked about what happened at Celebici with Mr Babic; is that what you are telling this court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is that you are telling this court that you have never discussed what happened at Celebici with Mr Babic since August of 1992? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: If he says he has not seen him, how could he have discussed it with him?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am just not clear whether he is talking about whether he has seen him right now. My question goes back to August of 1992, and I would like an answer from him whether he has talked to Mirko Babic about what happened in Celebici since August of 1992, not just since he has been in The Hague. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Since when they were incarcerated together, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Your question is valid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I had no opportunity. He was not with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Since August of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Now you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said on May 22nd your sons were arrested and taken away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The older one, and the younger one was taken with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are your son's names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Danilo and Zoran Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry. I did not get the second name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the next day --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- you said that a neighbour of yours, Mr Emir Alic, invited you to his home to hide out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct. He said: "Let this wild thing pass", and I didn't know what he meant by "wild thing". So I did go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Emir Alic: is he Muslim, Croatian or Serbian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was one of your neighbours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim that he is living in Libya today. Is that what you are telling this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He left shortly thereafter, shortly after I came from the prison, and he had been there before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the truth is that he is still in the Konjic area right now, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really don't know. I have not heard from anyone, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were picked up in an armoured car. Is that what you claim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a van without windows.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it like that vehicle that was shown to you in the video earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the video --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it was all enclosed. You could not see except up front, where the driver was, but in the back you couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about your friends in your village. Most of the other Serbs in your village had weapons, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know. I was not meddling in these things. I was not paying attention to what was going on. I was working my land and minding my own business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So are you just farming your home now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr Gotovac, you know someone named Dusko Bendjo, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you mentioned his name earlier today, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew he was the Bosnian Serb responsible for distributing the arms amongst the SDS members, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not know that. He was in Bjelovcina and I was in Vinjiste, so I could not know, plus I was not interested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware that the military police had come through your village and made an announcement for everybody to turn over their arms, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know that. The military police found me at Emir's house, and they detained me and took me to Celebici, so I don't know if they came. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do know that the people that arrested you had the white belts on, and they were military police. They weren't Muslim forces, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. They had white belts but I don't know what forces they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were at Celebici you saw the guards in Celebici, but you also saw members of the HVO, TO and the military police, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were some HVO people, because they had the chequerboard on their sleeves and the other ones wore lilies on their sleeves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But they were all visible at Celebici, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see them much. There was no light in the hangar. Whoever came in, you could not recognise them. Those who were younger may have seen better, but I couldn't see much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That brings me to another question: you know, and you have told this court already, I believe, that in May of 1992 there was no electricity after dark at Celebici, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the beginning,. We were 22, and number 6, not at all. When I went to number 22 as a patient, we did not turn on the lights, but if the guards or somebody else would walk in, they would turn it on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were always in the dark in 22 and in hangar number 6, is that is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In the hangar always in the dark and when I was in 22 as a patient in the second part there was light. In the first part there was no light.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is your testimony, of course, today earlier, that you were in the infirmary, dispensary, building number 22, from early July through August 30th; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Number 22.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned that when you were brought into number 22 on May 23rd that you met another prisoner named Spasoje Miljevic. I am sorry. I massacre these names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Miljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not testify whether he came with you in the car or not, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw them when they stepped out of the vehicle, because I could not see them inside, and then I said: "You came in the same vehicle?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he came in the same armoured car at the same time on the same day that you did; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on 23rd May 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified earlier that part of the mistreatment that you had seen at Celebici was Slobodan Babic; is that what you testified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When he was being arrested -- when he was arrested, he couldn't -- his eyesight was damaged, and he could only moan, and he was taken away, and Petko Grubac claims that he died in 8th March, school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But when you arrived in Celebici, Slobodan Babic, was he in building number 22 with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was several days, maybe up to five days. I can't recall precisely, because it was so tightly packed. We could only hear him. He was moaning, and I don't know how to call the sounds, but it was very difficult to see, because it was a small room with a lot of people in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The truth is that Mr Slobodan Babic was beaten before you have ever arrived in Celebici, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, before, before, when he was being detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know or could have known from the others that he was beaten at Radava and not in Celebici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is what Mirko Babic said, because they were brought together to Konjic to the hall in Konjic, where they were separated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know for a fact that Slobodan Babic was beaten before he ever arrived in Celebici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Havala.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you described building number 22. At the same time that you were in there on May 23rd, you were -- it was not used as an infirmary or a dispensary, was it? It was a holding place, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Looking at the pumps and hoses, it looked like a fire-fighting equipment storage room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But basically people were just placed in this building until they had a chance to be interviewed by the authorities to determine what their status was at the camp; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I honestly don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you had an interview while you were in building number 22, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that interview you were moved to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But only briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and they asked you important questions like were you a members of the SDS and did you have arms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't recall about the arms. I always said the same. I did not, and so nobody forced me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking whether anybody forced you. I just was trying to ask what kind of questions were asked of you. On that day that you had your interview you said you signed a statement, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I signed something, but I don't know what it was. Two young men showed up when I was questioned and they asked me a few more questions, and then they told me: "You don't recall this?" I said "I don't." They said: "Sign this", and I did but I don't know what. I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you did not know what this document was you signed because you did not have your glasses with you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have glasses and I could not see, so I don't know what the document was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your entire stay at Celebici you did not get any new glasses either, did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: How could he get them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You were not given a hearing-aid during the whole time you were at Celebici, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your Honours, are we quitting today at 5.30 or at 6? It will just determine whether I play a videotape now or whether I save it. Do you have any preference for today or should I just go on with some questions? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: We are closing any time now.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will just go with a few questions then. Thank you. You talked about Spasoje Miljevic being beaten while you were in number 22; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say that he was beaten, all you know for a fact from your own personal knowledge is that he was taken out by some guards and he was brought back in the same condition that he left in. Is that what your testimony is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not in the same condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Havala.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now in May of 1992 this person, Esad Landzo, or Zenga that you have referred to many times through your testimony today, he was not present or anywhere around building number 22, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was seriously ill when I came from number 6. I only heard him once, and I recognised the voice, and I could not see, because the door was closed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He was in building number 22 twice, first when he went there. Then he was moved to building number 6. Then he again after he was injured he again went to building number 22. So you have to specify to what period you are referring.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: You are absolutely right. I am sorry. I forget. The first time you were in building number 22, when you were waiting to be interviewed, before you went to hangar number 6; you have never saw Mr Landzo in May, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not. The first few days I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Havala.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you did not really see Mr Landzo until the middle part of June, after you had been moved to hangar number 6; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is right, the middle of June. That is when my turn came for this torture.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified that on May 26th, when you were in hangar number 22, a group of prisoners from Bradina were brought in. Is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. You could hear moans. The Golgotha that we barely survived. It was horrible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in building number 22 at the time, right, and those prisoners were not brought there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Number 9, number 6, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is your testimony to this court that the prisoners you are talking about from Bradina were taken to tunnel 9 or hangar number 6, but they did not come to building 22; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know the people, so I wouldn't know. It was so packed and it was so dark, but for the most part they were in numbers 9 and 6 and in some tunnel. I don't know where that tunnel was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that earlier that you had told Ms McHenry that you cannot hear so well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I don't hear that well. It is better now with these earphones, but otherwise it's not so good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is your testimony that on May 26th you heard these people in tunnel Number 9 or hangar number 6 singing Cetnik songs and using Muslim and Ustasha greetings, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear, and they were singing songs, but I don't know what songs they were, but you could hear them singing, and then somebody is in front of them and says "that" and then they repeat after that. So "ready" and "Praise the Lord", something religious. I could not recognise that very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that brings to mind another question: you say on May 26th you knew that the prisoners came from Bradina, but the next night another group of prisoners were brought in on May 27th and you did not know where they were from. What's the difference? How did you know the ones from Bradina and you did not know the ones the next night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bradina, that we found out in number 6 because some were moved from number 6 to Number 9 and the other way, so then we heard from them that it was on 26th, 27th May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your testimony about hearing the people from Bradina on May 26th is a result of your discussions with the other prisoners after you got to hangar number 6; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Ms McHenry --

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: McMurrey. We are all Irish or Scottish. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: I think this would be a convenient place to stop now, so tomorrow morning you will continue, instead of hurrying over your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr Gotovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You are welcome: thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Before we rise I think there are a few things we want to dispose of. Remember we have these witnesses protecting, protective measures and we have not indicated resolution of the argument. Now to make matters tidy so that you will be familiar with how to deal with the witnesses, we have considered the arguments on both sides and you remember we had two sets of motions: one, the first one, where you had A, B, C, D, E and F; then the second in which you have M to N. Now the second motion -- we took both of them together -- the second one you still are investigating, as you admitted, that somebody went to -- somebody was trying to investigate about witnesses in this Celebici case. That was the anxiety and the fear about those witnesses M to N. Now the other witnesses, witnesses C-B, C, D, E and F, we categorise them, and the category we have, the first category of witnesses which dealt mainly with the question of those who we certify. There were those which we felt did not really need complete anonymity. They did not really need a closed session, although perhaps they might require some image-distorting or voice-altering devices to enable them to be heard, but with respect to witness C, whose evidence involved sexual assault on him, we felt he should testify in closed session. Now witnesses D, E, F and G, up to M: we regard them to be able to testify in open session where their names and identity will be disclosed and, as I said, with image distoring and voice-altering devices to enable cross-examination relating to the identification which will not be allowed as long as they are cross-examined, but they should not be cross-examined relating to their identity and their names. Now, the witness B was a most anxious one. We have discovered that in all the prosecution's view the of witness B is that he does not want to meet the accused persons, although he knows that they cannot identify him by name merely. So even if he disclosed his name, they would not identify him. Now the prosecution has told us that the witness does not want to see the accused persons and also does not want them to see him. So merely indicating his name in the circumstances will almost amount to anonymity, because they cannot identify him, even if they saw him, except other factors are there. But the reason why this anonymity is being deserved the prosecution said is on a telephone conversation. He learned that this witness is likely to suffer from real traumatisation if he saw them or if they saw him, whichever way. I think in that respect the only evidence of that is the idea of the prosecutor and nothing more. Traumatisation is a medical condition which cannot be offered in that manner. So we did not think it is sufficient evidence to support that claim. Now, the suggestion that the witness should testify from the remote room was refused, because it might make matters more complicated, because the right of the accused persons to cross-examine him under Article 21(4)(e) is very clear. Apart from that, the nature of his evidence has not been disclosed, and none of the tests which have been formulated in the Tadic case, which we all know, have not been applied to this witness. So in all the circumstances it is difficult to justify the type of anonymity which has been given to him. So we rejected the prosecution's application. In order not to leave him bare, we still think he will testify in the courtroom to enable the accused persons to see him, but a screen will be built around him to prevent him from seeing the accused persons. That is the trauma that is avoided. That might help him, but the accused persons are entitled to cross-examine him and they are entitled not to lose their rights merely because he claims to be traumatised. So we will soon hand down our decisions but this is in the main line the disposition of the application before us. Now the next thing is we have a few announcements about a short vacation. You know that Easter is approaching, and we are not likely to sit on 28th and 31st March, and we will also not be sitting from 4th to about 11th or so of April. We will resume sitting on 14th April, but in between we will still be sitting. Just to give you advance information so that you will tidy your timetable and your arrangements. So the Trial Chamber will now rise until tomorrow. (5.35 pm)
